english: Whoever speaks a lie to the king, let his word not be heard again, and let him go out of the village. Whoever hears a lie and tells it to the king, let there be a reward for him. The word of a free man is dear to the sky.
uncertain: mē ḱléwseto: read as middle s-aorist injunctive 'let it not be heard'; could be 'not be famed'

english: If a dog kills a pig in the enclosure, let its (the dog's) mistress give a sheep to the son. If it kills a wolf, let him give nothing. If a dog eats a ?lamb of the sheep, let him ?call/drive it away.
uncertain: h₁ésyo pótnih₂: whose mistress, and why 'to the son' (suHnówey) is unclear
h₂éwim vs h₂ówim in the same item: e-grade/o-grade inconsistency

english: If a man leads a sister home (as wife), let him give the bride-price to her mother. She shall be free. If he does not pay it, let the mother lead the sister back.
uncertain: swésorm̥ 'sister' used for an unrelated woman, or 'his sister'?

english: Whoever seizes a sheep from the pen, he is a thief. If he seizes an eagle, let him give a horse to the king. Whoever lets a sheep go away from the pen, let him build the pen. The eagle is dear to the sky.
Let no one plough the sisters' field. If a man ploughs it, let him take/pay two of his yokes. If his cows enter the field and eat, let him work wool for her.
uncertain: wéyḱonti 3pl + h₁édeti 3sg with plural gʷówes: agreement looks wrong
h₁opéyetu 'work, make' + h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m 'wool': read as 'make good with wool'

english: I go to the water. The gods have seen my heart. My word is not a lie. If I lie, may the snake devour me. If I do not lie, may the water carry me out. I have not been afraid.
uncertain: déywōs read as nom.pl 'gods' (lengthened grade?) with dedr̥ḱé 3sg perfect: number mismatch?
dedwóyh₂e 1sg perfect 'I fear/I am not afraid'
